Chapter 7: Integrating the Five Principles in Daily Practice
So, you’ve wrapped your head around the five dysfunctions—now what? The real magic happens when you start weaving these principles into the everyday life of your team.
But let’s be honest, that’s where the challenge kicks in. It’s not just a box you check once and forget about.
Think of this process as a loop, not a straight line. Teams can slip. Maybe trust starts to fade, or people avoid tough conversations. Accountability? Sometimes it just slides off the radar.
The secret is to catch those shifts early, before they settle in and become the new normal.
So, how do you actually make the five principles a living, breathing part of your daily routine?
Here are some practical ways to keep your team on track:
First, hold regular retrospectives. Set aside a little time to look back—what’s working, and where might old dysfunctions be sneaking in?
Next, try rotating your meeting facilitators. Letting different team members lead the discussion gives everyone a sense of ownership.
And don’t underestimate the power of checklists and simple reminders. They’re great for keeping those five principles front and center, especially during meetings or big decisions.
Imagine starting your meeting with a quick trust-building exercise, or wrapping up with a round of peer feedback.
These little rituals? They help reinforce the culture you want, making it easier to tackle issues as soon as they pop up.
Now, leaders have a big part to play here. When they show vulnerability, invite healthy debate, clarify commitments, support accountability, and celebrate wins, it sets the tone for everyone.
But it’s not just on the leader—everyone has a role. High-performing teams are built on shared responsibility.
Over time, these habits become second nature. The team starts moving in sync—open communication, productive conflict, and real support for each other just become part of the rhythm.
And when challenges show up? Instead of fear or finger-pointing, the team meets them with resilience and creativity.
That’s what integration looks like—one step at a time, every day.
